title: Liam Rosenior says Robert Sanchez has reacted well to being dropped, insists No 1 role up for grabs
content:
Liam Rosenior has spoken to Robert Sanchez after the Chelsea keeper was left disappointed at being dropped for the game against Aston Villa in midweek.

Sanchez appeared to pay the price for a disappointing display in the 2-1 defeat at Arsenal last Sunday as he was replaced by Filip Jorgensen at Villa Park. The only other Premier League game he has not started this season was at Manchester City in January due to a muscular injury.

Rosenior spoke about the decision before Chelsea’s 4-1 win over Aston Villa, making it clear he does not have an “outright No 1”.

When asked if he had spoken to Sanchez about it, Rosenior replied: “I already have done. I’ve been really honest with Rob. He was really disappointed not to play the game, which I expect for every player, whether they’re a goalkeeper or an outfield player.

“But the way Rob responded in training, the way he responded in terms of supporting Filip, in terms of the warm-up, in terms of in the dressing room, was magnificent. There was no difference in it.

“If we’re going to be successful in the short and long term, you need a group, you need a squad with the right mentality. And Rob, so far, has been absolutely magnificent in that.”

Chelsea take on Wrexham in the FA Cup Fifth Round tomorrow night and there will be a lot of attention on whether Sanchez gets recalled or if Jorgensen keeps his place.

“I look at the goalkeeper position maybe differently in each game,” Rosenior added. “I want there to be competition in every area of the pitch. I know traditionally if there’s a change of goalkeeper, it’s like he’s now the No 1. It’s not the case.

“Filip has been working for his opportunity. I thought he took his opportunity really, really well. He was a massive influence in the (Aston Villa) game in terms of our build structure and how we created chances. He put in a really good performance. Rob’s put in great performances as well. But I want there to be competition in every area of the pitch.”

Pedro Neto will return from suspension for the tie but Estevao Willian and Jamie Gittens are still not ready to make their comebacks from hamstring injuries.
